transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sara Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Ellen Cho (CISO, Helios), Mark Rivers (Head of Platform), Priya Shah (Dir Eng)

Summary (auto): quick security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private options; primary concerns are SOC2/ISO compliance, SSO/SAML integration with Okta, RBAC and audit log retention, encryption & KMS, and data retention policies. Customer wants to evaluate Hosted for speed but needs to validate controls; dedicated/private are gating if Hosted can't meet residency/KMS needs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sara Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sara, AE at Redwood, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:04] Ellen Cho: Hi Sara, thanks. Good. We've been looking at Redwood based on the benchmark decks you shared. I'm Ellen, CISO at Helios.
[00:08] Mark Rivers: Mark here. Head of Platform, curious about networking and the dedicated/private options.
[00:11] Priya Shah: Priya, director of eng, I'll be doing the integration work.
[00:14] Sara Patel: Great, quick agenda: run through your security posture needs, talk through Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, cover SOC2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs and encryption, and then agree next steps. Sound good?
[00:20] Ellen Cho: Yep. We're time boxed to 45 so let's keep to that.
[00:25] Diego Martinez: Cool. To start, can you give us a sense of where Helios is today on compliance — SOC2? ISO? Any required certs?
[00:33] Ellen Cho: We are SOC2 Type II plus ISO 27001 in progress. SOC2 report is internal, but we do push out attestations to partners. For third-party platforms we evaluate their SOC2 and if it's Type II that's a baseline.
[00:43] Sara Patel: Understood. Redwood has a SOC2 Type II report and we've got an ISO 27001 summary — happy to share both. The Hosted API sits under our org-level controls; we can provide the standard artifacts, ASVs, penetration test summary, that sort of thing.
[00:53] Mark Rivers: Two things: data residency and key management. For some PII flows we need keys under our control, and some data must stay in our EU region. How do those map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[01:03] Diego Martinez: Good question. Short answer: Hosted is easiest to spin up and is our multi-tenant cloud offering — it supports region pinning to an extent but doesn't give you customer-managed KMS by default. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools where we can support customer-managed KMS through HSM/KMS integrations and stricter tenancy; Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you full control — network, KMS, and data residency, but requires more ops.
[01:20] Priya Shah: So for Hosted, if we need customer KMS, that's a blocker?
[01:24] Diego Martinez: Hosted doesn't offer direct customer KMS on day one — we do envelope encryption and manage the keys. We can discuss Bring Your Own Key for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have at-rest AES-256 and in-transit TLS 1.2+; but we know some customers need BYOK for regulated data.
[01:36] Ellen Cho: Okay that matches our expectation. SOC2 is fine for baseline but we need KMS integration for production PII workloads. Also need strong audit trails — we keep 7 years of logs for certain flows. How long do you retain audit logs and can we export them?
[01:47] Sara Patel: We maintain audit logs in Redwood Console; retention defaults to 90 days for hosted tiers, and longer retention is an add-on. Export is supported — you can push to S3 or a SIEM via a connector. For Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention and direct integrations to your logging stack.
[02:00] Mark Rivers: Push to S3 is good. Can those logs be delivered to our own bucket in our account?
[02:04] Diego Martinez: For Dedicated and Private, yes — you can configure delivery to your S3. For Hosted we have a managed export to Redwood-owned buckets by default but can set up cross-account delivery for enterprise plans.
[02:16] Ellen Cho: What about SSO? We run Okta with SAML and SCIM for user provisioning. Need SSO for the console and RBAC that maps to our groups.
[02:24] Sara Patel: Redwood supports SSO with SAML and SCIM for provisioning. Our RBAC is role-based with custom roles possible on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have predefined roles and group-mapping via SCIM. We can map Okta groups to Redwood roles.
[02:36] Priya Shah: Any gotchas on SCIM? We use group nesting and custom attributes.
[02:41] Diego Martinez: SCIM mostly supports flat groups; nested groups can be handled via Okta rules to flatten them. Custom attributes are supported but sometimes need a short mapping script. We'll share a sample metadata XML and a notes doc.
[02:52] Ellen Cho: Encryption in transit and at rest okay. KMS: can you confirm support for AWS KMS and also on-prem HSM? We use AWS KMS in primary cloud.
[03:01] Diego Martinez: We support AWS KMS for Dedicated and Private when deployed in AWS. For on-prem HSMs, Private on-prem can integrate with your HSM via standard KMIP or partner integrations — it'll be part of the architecture work. Hosted uses our managed key material.
[03:12] Sara Patel: Also to call out: Redwood supports customer-managed causal keys for embeddings? (laughter) Sorry, bad phrasing. What I mean — key wrap/envelope encryption patterns for model artifacts and logs.
[03:22] Mark Rivers: (laugh) no worries. Another important item: auditability for model access — who called which model, token-level cost, and traces.
[03:29] Diego Martinez: Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and per-route/model dashboards. All requests include request IDs and we log caller identity if authenticated via API keys or SSO. For stricter auditing we can forward logs including request metadata to your SIEM.
[03:41] Ellen Cho: Good. How about data deletion and retention — are there deletion APIs? If a user requests deletion, how do you handle training data and cached prefixes?
[03:49] Sara Patel: We have data retention policies configurable per-customer. For Hosted we support end-user deletion requests per our policy; prefix/KV cache TTLs can be set and there's a purge API for customer data. For Dedicated/Private you get full control to implement retention and deletion in your environment.
[04:04] Priya Shah: Need to confirm the SLA and RTO for deletion — we have regulatory requirements to ensure deletion within X days.
[04:10] Diego Martinez: We'll capture that as a follow-up; the specifics depend on how data is stored for the workload. For example, cache-only vs persisted logs. We'll add that to the action items.
[04:19] Mark Rivers: Any independence for pen tests / third party audit? Do you allow our third-party assessor to validate controls in Dedicated?
[04:25] Sara Patel: For Hosted we provide SOC2/pen test summaries. For Dedicated and Private, customers can arrange onsite/remote assessments under an NDA — typical for enterprise contracts.
[04:34] Ellen Cho: On legal side, we need data processing agreements + subprocessor list.
[04:38] Sara Patel: Yep, we have a DPA and a current subprocessor list — I'll send those.
[04:42] Priya Shah: On architecture: if we went Dedicated, what's the network layout? We need to know VPC peering, NAT, egress controls.
[04:49] Diego Martinez: Typical Dedicated pattern: we provision a dedicated cluster in your cloud account or our managed dedicated tenancy; connectivity via VPC peering or PrivateLink; egress can be restricted via security groups and NAT; we provide a network diagram. For Private on-prem, it's basically your network. I'll prepare a sample VPC diagram.
[05:03] Ellen Cho: Last question: data residency — we need EU-only for some customers. Can Hosted be ISO/EU only?
[05:09] Sara Patel: We have region pinning on Hosted but it's not absolute isolation; for strict EU-only workloads we recommend Dedicated in an EU region or Private. We'll document the isolation guarantees.
[05:19] Mark Rivers: Pricing-wise, if we need Dedicated and BYOK, what's the onboarding timeline?
[05:23] Sara Patel: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 6-8 weeks including legal and infra, possibly longer for BYOK/HSM integration. Hosted can be immediate for evaluation.
[05:30] Ellen Cho: Okay that helps. Seems like Hosted for initial eval, but Dedicated/Private likely for prod if we need BYOK or EU isolation.
[05:37] Sara Patel: Great — to recap next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, the DPA and subprocessor list, SAML/SCIM integration guide, VPC/network diagram, and sample retention/KMS options. Diego will follow up with a technical checklist and schedule the deep dive.
[05:52] Priya Shah: We'll share our infra diagram and retention policy by Monday.
[05:56] Sara Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll schedule the SE deep dive for next week — look for a calendar invite.
[06:01] Ellen Cho: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on quality: Some auto-transcription misheard acronyms ("sock two" for SOC2, "KV cash" for KV cache) and may have minor speaker attribution errors.
